title: Web and product analytics
for: traffic, sessions, conversions, funnels, retention, session replay

manual.export: Open the report in the analytics tool (GA4: Reports > Explore or a standard report; PostHog and Mixpanel: the insight), export it as CSV from the report's share or export menu, and drop the file into the snapshots folder.

vendors.name: Google Analytics 4
caveats: Experimental, local stdio only (Python via pipx); there is no remote endpoint and no Claude connector

Auth is Application Default Credentials: `gcloud auth application-default login --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` for a person, or a service-account JSON at GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS for an unattended run; GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID is the Cloud project with the Analytics Data and Admin APIs enabled
Tools: run_report, run_funnel_report, run_realtime_report, get_account_summaries, get_property_details, list_google_ads_links
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS and GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID are file path and project id, not secrets; the service-account file itself is the secret

auth.where: Google Cloud console: a service account with Viewer on the GA4 property, its JSON key on disk; or gcloud ADC for a person

cli.notes: auth only (application-default login); gcloud has no GA4 reporting command, so schedules use a script

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; a service account calls the Analytics Data API runReport (analyticsdata.googleapis.com) for the weekly traffic snapshot

vendors.name: PostHog
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__posthog`) until checked, or keep ?readonly=true in the URL (the header x-posthog-read-only: true does the same); the entries below pin it
?features=... and ?tools=... in the URL narrow the tool list further
The remote server routes US and EU automatically; a personal API key with the 'MCP Server' preset scopes is the headless path
Listed in the Claude connectors directory

auth.where: PostHog: Settings > Personal API keys, preset 'MCP Server' (a phx_ key)

cli.notes: posthog-cli api runs any endpoint and HogQL query with JSON output; run `posthog-cli api --agent-help` first; the route for scripted, scheduled pulls

script.notes: usually unnecessary: a workflow step runs posthog-cli and saves the JSON as a snapshot; a stdlib script posting to /api/projects/{id}/query is the fallback

vendors.name: Mixpanel
caveats: Read-only report tools; OAuth only
EU and India residency use https://mcp-eu.mixpanel.com/mcp and https://mcp-in.mixpanel.com/mcp
Listed in the Claude connectors directory
A scheduled pull uses the Query API with a service account (basic auth), so it lands in a script

auth.where: browser grant on first use (EU residency)

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; a service account (Organization Settings > Service Accounts) calls the Query API /api/query/insights for a scheduled snapshot

vendors.name: Amplitude
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__amplitude`) until checked
Writes create charts, dashboards and cohorts; no event data is written
The Claude connectors directory lists it for Claude but not Claude Code; the URL entry below works in Claude Code as a custom server
EU residency uses https://mcp.eu.amplitude.com/mcp

auth.where: browser grant on first use (EU residency)

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the project API key and secret key (Settings > Projects) call the Dashboard REST API /api/2/events/segmentation with basic auth for a scheduled snapshot

vendors.name: Plausible
caveats: community server maintained by Sentry (getsentry/plausible-mcp); judge as a script, not a vendor tool

Plausible ships no official MCP server; Sentry hosts this one at https://plausible-mcp.sentry.dev and it passes your Plausible API key straight through as a bearer token (no secret stored on their side)
Self-hosted Plausible needs a PLAUSIBLE_BASE_URL, which the hosted bridge does not take; run the repo locally for that

auth.where: Plausible: Settings > API keys (Stats API key)

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the Stats API v2 (/api/v2/query) is one POST per report and the simplest scheduled route

vendors.name: Matomo
caveats: Built into Matomo Cloud; on-premise installs add the 'MCP Server' plugin from the Marketplace
The endpoint URL is instance-specific and shown in the info box next to the MCP Server setting in Matomo's administration, so there is no committed entry; a person copies it from there when wiring

Auth is a Matomo API token (Administration > Personal > Security > Auth tokens) or OAuth 2.0; the FAQ says OAuth access tokens expire hourly and the plugin does not refresh them, so use the token; the header format is not printed on the FAQ
Any client holding the token reads what that user can read; rotate it periodically

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the Reporting API (index.php?module=API&method=VisitsSummary.get&format=csv) already returns CSV

vendors.name: Adobe Analytics / Customer Journey Analytics
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__adobe-cja`) until checked

GA since May 2026 and listed in the Claude connectors directory, but the overview page omits the endpoint URL and auth flow (Adobe IMS assumed); no .mcp.json entry until a person reads them from the Adobe Developer Console
Writes manage segments and components, not data

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; an Adobe Developer Console project with OAuth server-to-server credentials calls the CJA Reporting API /reports for a scheduled snapshot

vendors.name: Microsoft Clarity
caveats: Local stdio server (microsoft/clarity-mcp-server, npm @microsoft/clarity-mcp-server) over the Clarity data export API; read-only
The token is passed as a command-line argument (--clarity_api_token), which shows in the process list on shared machines; the env-placeholder keeps it out of the file
The data export API returns up to three days of data per call

auth.where: Clarity: Settings > Data Export > Generate new API token

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the same token calls the data export API (www.clarity.ms/export-data/api/v1/project-live-insights) for a scheduled snapshot

vendors.name: Heap and Hotjar (Contentsquare)
caveats: No standalone Heap or Hotjar server was found; a Contentsquare MCP that covers both is mentioned only on a competitor's comparison page and could not be verified on Contentsquare's own docs
Until a vendor page exists, use the manual export or a generic connector
